query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a lamellar dual-phase microstructure through tailored thermo-mechanical processing can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a single solid-solution phase
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing to introduce a lamellar dual-phase microstructure
generation.structural_mediator: Lamellar dual-phase microstructure with a combination of soft and ductile fcc phase and hard B2 phase
generation.mechanism: The introduction of a lamellar dual-phase microstructure leads to a combination of strength and ductility due to the synergetic reinforcement of the two phases, allowing for improved mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased strength and ductility compared to the single solid-solution phase alloy
generation.baseline: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a single solid-solution phase
generation.boundary: The introduction of a lamellar dual-phase microstructure may not be effective in all eutectic high-entropy alloys, and the optimal processing conditions may vary depending on the specific alloy composition.
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms by which the lamellar dual-phase microstructure improves strength and ductility are not fully understood and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without a lamellar dual-phase microstructure, introduced through tailored thermo-mechanical processing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of a lamellar dual-phase microstructure does not lead to a significant increase in strength and ductility compared to the single solid-solution phase alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. This work provides a pathway for strengthening eutectic alloys and widens the design toolbox for high-performance materials based upon EHEAs. Recent studies indicate that eutectic high-entropy alloys can simultaneously possess high strength and high ductility, which have potential industrial applications. The present study focuses on Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a lamellar dual-phase (fcc + B2) precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy. This alloy exhibits an fcc + B2 (B2 with bcc nano-precipitates) microstructure resulting in a combination of the soft and ductile fcc phase together with hard B2 phase. Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength. The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism. The alloy was tested under quasi-static (strain-rate = 10−3 s−1) tensile loading and dynamic (strain-rate = 103 s−1) compressive loading. Due to the fine lamellar microstructure with a large number of fcc-bcc interfaces, the alloy show relatively high flow-stresses, ~1400 MPa under quasi-static loading and in excess of 1800 MPa under dynamic loading. To tackle the aforementioned problems, eutectic HEAs (EHEAs) [] were proposed. On the one hand, EHEAs should have the general character of traditional eutectic alloys. In this sense, EHEAs should have better fluidity and thus better castability and less casting defects [,]. On the other hand, EHEAs as one kind of in-situ composites with lamellar or rod-like eutectic microstructures might reach the balance between strength and ductility via mixing the soft FCC phase with the hard BCC phase or intermetallic compound [,,,,,,,,]. Some EHEAs indeed have outstanding properties. Lu et al. [] reported the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA with simultaneous high strength (944 MPa) and good ductility (25.6%). The excellent mechanical properties do not depend significantly on derivation of eutectic compositions []. After cold-rolling and annealing, its strength reached up to 1.2 GPa and its elongation could remain at about 12% []. After cryo-rolling and annealing, its strength could reach up to 1.47 GPa while its ductility could even increase to 14% []. He et al. [,] designed the CoCrFeNiNbx EHEAs and found that the microstructures were stable from 600 °C to 900 °C.
